lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest-first.
items.because: The older Westfield State University role appears above the more recent Lumen Travel internship, which may confuse a recruiter scanning the chronology.

items.says: “Owned” does not show what you built, maintained, standardized, or changed, or what improved.
items.because: The line describes a duty rather than a concrete web-development contribution.

items.says: The strongest line is not the opening line.
“The findings led to” weakens your role in turning the interviews into preview mode.
The line incorrectly credits merely writing a checklist with reducing failed audits.
items.because: The reduction requires adoption, application, and remediation or other implementation work.

items.says: “Accessibility checklist” does not identify the practices it contained.
The search-time reduction does not clearly state its measurement type or unit.
The 35% performance improvement lacks a named metric and baseline, and the repeated “by” is clumsy.
The named changes overstate how all 14 accessibility issues were fixed.
items.because: Keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels cannot by themselves resolve every kind of audit finding.

items.says: The release-protection result is buried after “which caught.”
items.because: The testing method is more prominent than the outcome.

items.says: Lazy-loading the hero image is incorrectly credited with reducing LCP.
items.because: Lazy-loading a likely LCP element generally delays it rather than producing the stated improvement.

items.says: Storing input in React state before using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` does not prevent cross-site scripting.
items.because: React state does not sanitize user-controlled HTML, and unsafe markup can execute unless sanitized before rendering.

items.says: “Prevented cross-site scripting in comments” gives no measurement or evidence of its scope.
The strongest line is not the opening line.
“Showing live bus arrivals” omits how the data was obtained and delivered and what changed for riders.
items.because: The bullet shows adoption but leaves the technical integration and rider outcome to inference.

items.says: “Against 2.9s before” is an awkward comparison.
The bullet says React and TypeScript while the project heading says Vue.
items.because: The unexplained framework inconsistency makes the technology and contribution difficult to trust or place.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend” does not show the specific contribution or its scale.
items.because: A reader cannot distinguish substantial feature work from minor implementation assistance.

items.says: The supported cases do not show what improved, and “its tests” does not show how the implementation was verified.
The travel-search result is unrelated to the library project and appears to duplicate the Lumen Travel achievement.
items.because: It makes the project scope unclear and appears to restate the hotel-search result with different wording and figures.

items.says: “More than halving” and “about a tenth” are imprecise, and the booking metric and relative increase are unclear.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what bookings measures or reconcile the claim with the 9% A/B-test figure elsewhere.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: The error looks careless and can interfere with keyword matching.

items.says: Angular appears in Skills without an entry describing its use.
